abstract: Aiolos (Ikzf3), a member of the Ikzf family, has been primarily characterized in the immune system, whereas other Ikzf family members have reported roles in the brain and have been implicated in schizophrenia. However, the potential role of Aiolos in the brain remains broadly unexplored. Combining human samples, translational and gain and loss of function mouse models we characterized Aiolos expression in the brain and investigated its potential involvement in schizophrenia. Here we show that Aiolos expression varies across brain regions and developmental stages, stabilizing in principal neurons during adulthood. Moreover, we identified that Aiolos is dysregulated in peripheral immune cells and in the hippocampus of patients with schizophrenia. Modeling the impact of those dysregulations in mice induced behavioral phenotypes relevant to the positive, negative and cognitive symptoms of schizophrenia. Finally, we found that mimicking Aiolos hippocampal dysregulation in mice generated increased complement protein abundance, accompanied by microglia-associated loss of synaptic material. Our results suggest that Aiolos may regulate complement-mediated synaptic elimination with potential implications for schizophrenia.
